survey: A chunky handheld calculator floats on a flat orange background with no ground plane. The camera faces it almost head-on, with the body turned slightly in the picture plane (it leans clockwise) and tipped a little, so a sliver of thickness shows along the right and bottom edges and a highlight runs along the top-left bevel. Parts: a small red solar strip sits on the top edge, set in from the right. Below it is a large white display, an inset rectangle whose top and bottom edges run parallel to the body's top edge. Under that is a 4×4 key grid: three columns of dark-blue keys and one column of cyan operator keys on the right. The key rows slope up to the right like the body's top and bottom edges, and the columns lean like the body's left and right edges. Every key is a raised rounded cube, and each shows its side faces on the same sides (lower and right) as the body, so the extrusion direction matches the body's thickness. The keys are near-equal in size and spacing, which fits a face turned only slightly away from the camera. The body's top and bottom edges are about the same length and its long sides stay parallel, which suits a near-frontal view with little foreshortening. No round parts and no ground contact need checking.
